COMMON JUDGMENT:

1. The Appeal MACMA.No.214 of 2022 is filed by the appellants/claimants assailing the order,
dt.08.12.2021, in MVOP.No.2033 of 2015 and the Appeal in MACMA.No.225 of 2022 is filed by the appellants/claimants therein assailing the order, dt.08.12.2021, in MVOP.No.2031 of 2015, both passed by the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-XXVI Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad (for short 'the Tribunal'), whereby the Tribunal while awarding compensation in respective appeals, has restricted the liability of the 3rd respondent-Insurance Company to the extent of Rs.1,29,875/- each in both the claim petitions and directed the 1st and 2nd respondents therein to pay the remaining compensation.
2.

sentences.text: Though the claimants and the impugned awards are different, since the claims arose out of the same accident involving the very same vehicle, both these appeals are analogously heard and disposed of by this common judgment.

3. For the sake of convenience and for better understanding, the deceased in MACMA.No.214 of 2022 is hereinafter referred to as deceased-1 and deceased in MACMA.No.225 of 2022 is hereinafter referred to as deceased-2.

Brief facts of both the appeals:
4. The claimants filed respective claim petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-(MACMA.No.214 of 2022) for the death of the deceased-1 and Rs.20,00,000/- (MACMA.No.225 of 2022) for the death of deceased-2.
5.

On the fateful day, i.e., on 23.06.2015, while both the deceased persons were in their house in Chinna Thimmapur(Vontimamidi), Mulugu Mandal, Medak District, which is abutting to Rajiv Rahadari, the driver of JCB bearing No.TS 10 EC 1459, without any prior information and notice to the abutting house owners of Rajiv Rahadari, was attending to the construction work of drainage canal abutting the house of the deceased persons and while carrying on the work of removing the old Mohammed Rajeeya Bee And Another vs K. Balvanth Reddy And 2 Others on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108509304/
3 structures abutting the house of the deceased, operated the JCB in a rash and negligent manner, due to which the bucket of the JCB dashed the roof of both deceased persons' house, due to which their roof collapsed and fell on the both deceased persons, which resulted the deceased persons getting crushed under the fallen roof and died on the spot.
6.

sentences.text: Further, the police, Mulugu, Medak District, had registered a case in Crime No.70 of 2015 against the driver of JCB bearing No.TS 10 EC 1459 and conducted investigation.

7. The claimants (in both claim petitions) contended that as on the date of incident, deceased-1 was aged about 52 years, hale, healthy and working as Plantation Watcher in Forest Development Corporation, and earning Rs.12,000/- p.m., while deceased-2 was aged about 30 years, hale, health and running hotel business as well as doing tailoring work, and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.; that on account of the untimely death of the deceased persons, the claimants in both the claim petitions suffered mental agony and thus claimed compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- and Rs.20,00,000/-
respectively.

It is further contended that respondent No.1 and 2 being the driver and owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.3 being the insurer, are jointly and severally liable to compensation to the claimants.
8. The respondents No.1 and 2 remained absent and did not choose to file counters or choose to participate in trial before the learned Tribunal.

9. The respondent No.3 filed counter before the Tribunal denying the manner of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle, ownership of the respondents No.1 and 2 and insurance of the offending with the said respondent and further denied that the 1st respondent was having valid and subsisting driving license to drive the vehicle and that the road was roadworthy to ply and having permit to drive at the place of incident.

So also claimed that the compensation amount and interest claimed are excessive and exorbitant and prayed to dismiss the petitions and also stated that as per the policy, the liability of the respondent No.3 is restricted by the contract to the extent of Rs.2,59,750/- and to that extent only the respondent No.3 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
10.
The claimants in both the claim petitions filed rejoinders denying the counter averments reiterating the petition averments and claimed Rs.5,00,000/- towards damages of the house 11.

The Tribunal has framed following similar issues in both the MVOPs, except for the change of the name of the deceased:
"1) Whether the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the JCB bearing No.TS-10-EC- 1459 causing death of Syed Jalal Bee Alias Jalal Begum?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

12. The Tribunal, has also framed following additional issue in both the claim petitions:
"Whether the accident that took place was not a motor vehicle accident?

13. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Ex.A1 to A6 were marked on behalf of the claimants and RW1 was examined and Ex.B1 was marked on behalf of the respondents in respect of MACMA.No.214 of 2022 and PW1 was examined and Ex.A1 to A6 were marked on behalf of the claimants and RW1 was examined and Ex.B1 was marked on behalf of the respondents in respect of MACMA.No.225 of 2022.

14. The Tribunal after elaborate hearing and enquiry partly allowed the claims in both the claim petitions, holding that the vehicle i.e., JCB/Crane is a motor vehicle able to move and duly registered with the concerned Regional Transport Authority by a valid registration number, thus the accident was a motor vehicle accident, and occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, which resulted in the death of the deceased-1 and deceased-2.

The Tribunal however restricted the liability of the 3rd respondent to the extent of Rs.1,29,875/- each in both the claim petitions holding that Ex.B1 policy is a limited policy covering the limit to the extent of Rs.2,59,750/- as the insurance policy was a contract entered between the insured and the insurer,
which is expressly restricted to the said amount, and directed the 1st and 2nd respondents to pay the remaining compensation in both the claim petitions i.e., Rs.12,05,125/- in MVOP.No.2033 of 2015 and Rs.13,33,725/- in MVOP.No.2031 of 2015, respectively.

15. Challenging the quantum of compensation and decision of the Tribunal in restricting the liability of the 3rd respondent only to Rs.2,59,750/- and apportioning the same equally in both the claim petitions, the instant appeals are filed by the claimants.

16. Heard Sri P.Ramakrishna Reddy, learned counsel for the appellants, Sri Kota Subba Rao,
learned counsel for respondent No.2-owner and Sri Harinath Reddy Soma, learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.3-Insurance Company, in both the appeals 17.

Now that the Tribunal has categorically held that the offending vehicle is responsible for the accident, which resulted in two deaths, and awarded compensation against the respondents,
however restricted the liability of the 3rd respondent to the tune of Rs.1,29,875/- in each claim petition, and the balance amount of compensation was directed to be paid and recovered from respondent Nos.1 & 2.
18.

Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal erred in restricting the compensation to the third party liability mentioned in the insurance policy i.e., Ex.B1, despite a specific clause mentioned under 'Third Party Liability' that the 3rd respondent will indemnify the insurer without any restriction and the Tribunal failed to appreciate the said aspect.

He further contended that the Tribunal has erred in considering the income of both the deceased on lower side and also failed to consider the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Mohammed Rajeeya Bee And Another vs K. 19.

Per contra, learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company contended that as both the deceased were third parties to the contract executed and agreed between the insured and the insurer vide Ex.B1/Policy and it also governs the third party liability to a limited extent, the Tribunal has rightly restricted the liability on the 3rd respondent to the amount limited in Ex.B1 policy and apportioned the same into two equal halves and granted the amounts, and that the amounts as awarded by the Tribunal under different heads are just and reasonable and needs no interference.
20.
I have given earnest consideration to the submissions made on either side and perused the material on record.

21. The facts on record clearly establish that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of (2017) 16 SCC 680 the JCB bearing No.TS-10-EC-1459 and that the deaths of deceased-1 and deceased-2 arose out of the use of the said motor vehicle.
The finding of the Tribunal that it was a motor vehicle accident has attained finality, as there is no appeal by the insurer disputing negligence.

22. The only questions that needs to be considered in these appeals are (1) whether the Tribunal was justified in restricting the liability of the 3rd respondent-Insurance Company to Rs.1,29,875/- in each claim petition on the ground of limited third-party coverage under Ex.B1 policy, and (2)
whether
the compensation awarded is just and reasonable.
(1) Liability of the 3rd Respondent - Insurance Company 23.

The Tribunal restricted the liability of the insurer on the ground that Ex.B1 policy is a limited policy covering third-party risk only up to Rs.2,59,750/-, and therefore fixed only half of the said amount in each case.
Whether, such restriction is legally sustainable or not, is the foremost issue to be decided.
24. Firstly, the accident admittedly arose out of the use of the insured vehicle.
The deceased were third parties having no contractual relationship with the owner or insurer.

Under Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, an insurance policy covering third-party risk is statutorily required to indemnify the insured against liability incurred in respect of death or bodily injury to any person arising out of the use of a motor vehicle in a public place.

25. The expression "any person" has consistently been interpreted by the Courts to mean that third-party liability in respect of death or bodily injury is not subject to a monetary cap, unless specifically provided under the statute.
After the amendment to Section 147, the concept of limited liability in respect of third-party death or bodily injury no longer survives.
The insurer cannot contract out of its statutory liability so as to defeat the beneficial object of the legislation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Secondly, the policy clause relied upon by the Tribunal must be read harmoniously with the statutory mandate under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Even if the policy refers to a numerical limit, such a limitation cannot override the statutory requirement of covering unlimited third-party liability in cases of death or bodily injury.
27. In the present case, the insurer issued a valid policy covering third-party risk and has admitted the existence and coverage of the policy.
Therefore, it is bound to fully indemnify the insured in respect of the compensation awarded to third parties.

The relevant portion of the policy (Ex.B1)
reads as follows:
"THIRD PARTY LIABILITY:
It is hereby agreed and declared that notwithstanding anything to the contrary stated in this policy, the Company will indemnify the insured:
a) Against legal liability for the accidental loss or damage caused to the property of other persons.
b) Against legal liability(liability under contra excepted) for fatal or non-fatal injury to any person other than the insured or his own employees or employee of the owner of the works/site/premises/location or employees of the other Firms/connected with any other work site/premises/location or members of the family of the insured or any of the aforesaid.
28. A plain reading of the above clause makes it clear that the insurer undertook to indemnify the insured against third-party liability for fatal or non-fatal injuries.
29. Thirdly, the Motor Vehicles Act is a social welfare legislation enacted to ensure that innocent victims of motor accidents are not left without remedy.

Restricting the insurer's liability to a nominal sum and directing the claimants to recover the remaining substantial amount from the owner would defeat the very purpose of compulsory third-party insurance, especially, when there is no proof of breach of policy conditions such as absence of a valid driving licence or misuse of the vehicle.
30. Although the insurer-3rd respondent alleged breach of policy conditions, no convincing or reliable evidence was produced to substantiate the same.
There is nothing on record to show any willful or serious violation that would entitle the insurer to deny indemnification.
Hence, the insurer cannot escape its liability.

31. In National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Swaran Singh & Ors 2 the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as under:
"Concededly different types of insurance covers are issued containing different nature of contract of insurance.

32.

sentences.text:
Further, in Boya Devendrappa v. S.Farida Begum & Ors. 3 the Hon'ble High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Amavarati held as under:
"........The terms of contract between the insured and the insurer determining their rights and liabilities towards each other are not and should not be confused with the statutory liability of the insurer for the third party risk.

entities.text: Boya Devendrappa v. S.Farida Begum & Ors. 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Amavarati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: If there is a breach of contract on the part of the insured, the insurer may proceed against the insured.
As far as third party risk is concerned, the liabilities being statutory, it cannot be overridden by terms of the contract of insurance between the parties".
33. The above judgments make it clear that policy conditions cannot defeat the rights of third parties.
34. In view of the above legal and factual position, the Tribunal erred in restricting the liability of the 3rd respondent to Rs.1,29,875/- in each claim petition.

In cases involving third- party risks, the liability of the insurer is statutory and compulsory, and cannot be reduced by internal limitations in 3 MANU/AP/0305/2023 the policy and the insured and the insurer both cannot enter into an agreement to absolve their liability to indemnify the victim jointly and severally.
35. In the considered opinion of the Court, the Tribunal ought to have fixed joint and several liability on respondents 1 to 3, for the loss sustained by the third parties and the insurance policy/

Ex . B1,though restricted the liability of the insurance company, it is only against any damage or loss caused to the insured, and the insurance company cannot be absolvedfrom its liability to indemnify the third party, by restricting the amount and the findings of the Tribunal by fixing the liability on the respondent No.3 only to Rs.2,59,750/-i.e., Rs.1,29,875/- in each claim petition, as per Ex.B1 policy is perverse, untenable and are liable to be set aside and accordingly, set aside and the 1st point is answered accordingly, in favour of the appellants/claimants.

36. Thus, the findings of the Tribunal insofar as it restricted the liability of the 3rd respondent to Rs.1,29,875/-each in both the claim petitions is legally unsustainable, contrary to the settled position of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, and therefore liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, this point is answered in favour of the claimants.

(2) Just Compensation :
37.
Now that this Court has decided and answered point No.1, the next issue would be what would be the just and fair compensation.

opennyai_summary.issue:
The Tribunal has framed following similar issues in both the MVOPs, except for the change of the name of the deceased:
"1) Whether the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the JCB bearing No.TS-10-EC- 1459 causing death of Syed Jalal Bee Alias Jalal Begum?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so to what extent and from whom?
12. The Tribunal, has also framed following additional issue in both the claim petitions:
"Whether the accident that took place was not a motor vehicle accident?
22. The only questions that needs to be considered in these appeals are (1) whether the Tribunal was justified in restricting the liability of the 3rd respondent-Insurance Company to Rs.1,29,875/- in each claim petition on the ground of limited third-party coverage under Ex.B1 policy, and (2)
opennyai_summary.facts: 14. The Tribunal after elaborate hearing and enquiry partly allowed the claims in both the claim petitions, holding that the vehicle i.e., JCB/Crane is a motor vehicle able to move and duly registered with the concerned Regional Transport Authority by a valid registration number, thus the accident was a motor vehicle accident, and occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, which resulted in the death of the deceased-1 and deceased-2.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal erred in restricting the compensation to the third party liability mentioned in the insurance policy i.e., Ex.B1, despite a specific clause mentioned under 'Third Party Liability' that the 3rd respondent will indemnify the insurer without any restriction and the Tribunal failed to appreciate the said aspect.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Tribunal restricted the liability of the insurer on the ground that Ex.B1 policy is a limited policy covering third-party risk only up to Rs.2,59,750/-, and therefore fixed only half of the said amount in each case.
Whether, such restriction is legally sustainable or not, is the foremost issue to be decided.
The deceased were third parties having no contractual relationship with the owner or insurer.
Under Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, an insurance policy covering third-party risk is statutorily required to indemnify the insured against liability incurred in respect of death or bodily injury to any person arising out of the use of a motor vehicle in a public place.
25. The expression "any person" has consistently been interpreted by the Courts to mean that third-party liability in respect of death or bodily injury is not subject to a monetary cap, unless specifically provided under the statute.
After the amendment to Section 147, the concept of limited liability in respect of third-party death or bodily injury no longer survives.
The insurer cannot contract out of its statutory liability so as to defeat the beneficial object of the legislation.

6 26.
Secondly, the policy clause relied upon by the Tribunal must be read harmoniously with the statutory mandate under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Even if the policy refers to a numerical limit, such a limitation cannot override the statutory requirement of covering unlimited third-party liability in cases of death or bodily injury.
27. In the present case, the insurer issued a valid policy covering third-party risk and has admitted the existence and coverage of the policy.
Therefore, it is bound to fully indemnify the insured in respect of the compensation awarded to third parties.
29. Thirdly, the Motor Vehicles Act is a social welfare legislation enacted to ensure that innocent victims of motor accidents are not left without remedy.
Restricting the insurer's liability to a nominal sum and directing the claimants to recover the remaining substantial amount from the owner would defeat the very purpose of compulsory third-party insurance, especially, when there is no proof of breach of policy conditions such as absence of a valid driving licence or misuse of the vehicle.
There is nothing on record to show any willful or serious violation that would entitle the insurer to deny indemnification.
Hence, the insurer cannot escape its liability.
In cases involving third- party risks, the liability of the insurer is statutory and compulsory, and cannot be reduced by internal limitations in 3 MANU/AP/0305/2023 the policy and the insured and the insurer both cannot enter into an agreement to absolve their liability to indemnify the victim jointly and severally.
Ex .
